data.description:
# REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE pointer with per-key layering

## Context / Problem
CI and a local developer need different LLM configuration for the same checkout. Today the only
config sources are discovered by walking up from the repo root, so an environment cannot point rebar
at its own file without editing the repo's.

## Approach
Add `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`, naming a TOML file whose keys LAYER over the discovered config rather
than replacing it. Layering is deliberate: an environment overriding one key must not restate the
whole config, because that duplication is a likelier source of drift than precedence subtlety.
Precedence becomes: CLI `-c llm.KEY` > `REBAR_LLM_<KEY>` env > REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE > discovered
config file > default.

Prior art for the pointer itself: `KUBECONFIG`, `AWS_CONFIG_FILE`, `DOCKER_CONFIG` all use an env var
naming a config file. Those REPLACE; rebar layers, for the duplication reason above.

Secondary benefit: hermetic tests. Pointing at an empty file makes model resolution independent of
whatever `rebar.toml` is up-tree — the same trick `AWS_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null` provides for boto3.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` and/or `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` — the pointer and its layering.
- `tests/unit/` — precedence tests.

## Testing
Unit tier: config resolution only.
- a key present ONLY in the pointed file is used.
- a key present in BOTH is taken from the pointed file.
- a key present ONLY in the discovered file survives (this is what distinguishes layering from replace).
- env still beats the pointed file.
- a pointer naming a nonexistent file fails loudly rather than silently falling back.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts a key set only in the discovered config survives when the pointer supplies other keys
- [ ] a test asserts the pointed file wins per-key over the discovered config
- [ ] a test asserts `REBAR_LLM_<KEY>` env still beats the pointed file
- [ ] a test asserts a pointer to a missing path raises a typed rebar config error naming the variable
- [ ] `docs/env-vars.md` lists `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` after regeneration
